title: The Insider's Reveal — Jordan Kelley

fields.headline: Jordan Kelley Confesses to Insider Threat
fields.narration: The facilitator stands and addresses the group. 'Team, I need to be clear: Jordan Kelley is not just an IT manager. He is the threat. He planted a Raspberry Pi on the camera VLAN to intercept unencrypted payment data. He used the legacy server in Room 217 as a covert exfiltration node. The data was tunneling out via DNS to a remote C2 server. He claims he was blackmailed over a gambling debt — but he never reported it. He never sought help. He chose to act alone. The logs were altered, the door to Room 217 was propped open, and the network was compromised — all while he was on duty. The system did not fail. It was manipulated by someone who had full access and was trusted to keep it safe.'
keyFacts: Jordan Kelley is the insider who planted the MitM device on the camera VLAN.
The rogue device intercepted unencrypted payment data from the Retail VLAN.
Room 217 was used as a covert exfiltration node via a legacy server.
The data was tunneled out via DNS to a remote C2 server.
Kelley was under extortion pressure but failed to report the threat.
fields.expectedAction: Facilitator leads guided discussion on insider threat controls, separation of duties, and PCI compliance.
fields.facilitatorNote: Pause after the narration to allow the weight of the reveal to settle. Use the 'nudge' from I-13 as context for the group's prior failure to act. Emphasize that the network did not fail — it was compromised by a trusted insider.

instructorNote: This inject concludes the scenario. Use it to prompt reflection on trust, access control, and the human factor in cybersecurity. Watch for players who minimize Kelley's role or focus on technical fixes over process failures.
